subject: biotechnology
title: Fermentation: Yeast Converts Glucose to Ethanol and Carbon Dioxide

segments.say: Add yeast: living cells enter the glucose solution. Yeast is added to a flask of glucose solution, and the glucose bar is full - nothing has been converted yet, and there is no ethanol. Point at the empty gas space on your student notes before anything collects there.
questions: What is in the flask at this stage, and what is the glucose bar doing?

segments.say: Fermentation begins: glucose falls, ethanol and gas appear. The yeast takes in glucose, and as it is consumed the glucose bar begins to fall; ethanol appears in the liquid and carbon dioxide bubbles form, rise through the liquid and reach the gas space. Now try the gas question on your worksheet.
questions: What happens to the glucose bar as the products appear?
Which gas is produced, and where do its bubbles go?

segments.say: Conversion continues: glucose low, ethanol and gas grow. More glucose is converted: the glucose bar is low, the ethanol bar keeps rising, and more carbon dioxide bubbles rise and collect in the gas space. Check the bar order against your student notes before moving on.
questions: Why does the ethanol bar rise at the same time as the glucose bar falls?
What is collecting in the gas space, and where did it come from?

segments.say: Complete: glucose used up, ethanol and carbon dioxide produced. The glucose is almost gone because it was converted: the ethanol bar is high and the gas space is full of collected carbon dioxide - nothing appeared from nothing. Keep the whole conversion - glucose full, glucose falls, glucose low, glucose used up - in view as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
questions: What exactly happened to the glucose by the end?
What is the whole fermentation, in order?
segments.watchFor: The alcohol appears from nothing as the mixture ferments, because the glucose in the flask stays the same while ethanol and gas are produced. Listen for students who treat the ethanol and gas as created from nothing while the glucose stayed unchanged. Send them back to the bars: The yeast converts the glucose: as fermentation proceeds the glucose is used up, and that same material reappears as ethanol in the liquid and carbon dioxide gas collecting above it - glucose falls by the amount converted.
